response:
Diagnosis: eight generations have isolated one mechanism with unusual clarity. The valuation leg must be an *unencumbered claim* yield (net current assets less all liabilities, rank-combined with recurring cash earnings, both against market cap), and the conditioning variable must be *cash measured against the demands on cash*. Every cash-based gate on this leg works — che/cogs gives +6.3% (t=4.94), (che−lct)/cogs +5.0% (t=4.23), the min of runway and cash-to-debt +5.2% (t=4.17), cash-to-debt +4.9% (t=4.26) — and every non-cash gate on the identical leg fails: retained-earnings backing +1.4%, current-liability dependence +0.1%, cost-base stability −0.0%, gross profitability +2.4%, trough profitability +1.7%. The short side is equally strong but its cross-sectional slope stays flat (funding gap: −5.4%, t=−5.09, fmb −0.38), which is a portfolio-construction issue rather than an economic one. With one generation left after this, I test the four highest-value remaining questions — which claims on cash actually force the firm (S1), whether the runway is a stock or a flow concept (S3, S5), whether a broader cheapness consensus lifts the slope (S2) — plus the two-sided composite that unites the validated long and short mechanisms (S4) and one structural form test (S6).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Claim Cheapness With Cash After Commitments
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dlc, dvc)), cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: Only some current claims can actually force a firm to transact: debt maturing this year must be repaid and dividends are sticky commitments management will not cut without damage, whereas trade payables revolve with the business; cash net of the genuinely committed outflows, in months of operating cost, is the true measure of freedom.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive brackets this question — gross cash gives +6.3% and cash net of *all* current liabilities gives +5.0% — so subtracting only the committed subset tests directly which part of the near-term claim stack is economically binding, rather than rescaling either measure. Dividends and current debt are the two outflows a firm cannot defer without a market-visible failure, so the construct has a precise interpretation and remains defined for the many firms with neither.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Consensus Cheapness With Survival Horizon
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), SUMRANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: A discount is most credible when three independent accounting bases agree that the firm is cheap — its unencumbered balance-sheet claim, its recurring cash earnings and its gross profit stream — and such consensus cheapness, in a firm that cannot be forced to transact, should be the most reliably mispriced state.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gross-profit yield paired with the same runway gate produced the archive's largest cross-sectional slope (fmb 7.71) but only +2.9% alpha, while the claim-based leg produced the largest alpha (+6.3%) at a slope of 3.86; adding the profit channel as a third equally weighted rank tests whether the two sources of evidence can be captured together instead of traded off. Because the channels enter as ranks, no accounting magnitude dominates, and coverage stays at the level of the champion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Claim Cheapness With Extended Runway
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(che, MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3)), cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm's true survival horizon is the cash it holds plus the cash it earns each year, both measured against its operating cost base; a profitable cash-rich firm is effectively never forced, while an unprofitable one with the same cash balance is on a clock.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every archived gate uses the cash stock alone, so it cannot distinguish a firm whose buffer is being replenished from one whose buffer is being drained — the exact distinction that separates quality value from a trap on a finite countdown. Adding the three-year cash-earnings flow to the numerator keeps the months-of-operations interpretation and, unlike the flow term in the valuation leg, is scaled by costs rather than price, so it carries genuinely different information.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Unforced Cheapness Minus Forced Richness
EXPRESSION: SUB(MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(che, cogs))), MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(dlc, che), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: The same economics governs both tails: a cheap firm that nobody can force to transact is underpriced, and a richly priced firm facing a cash shortfall against maturing debt is overpriced; a single score that adds the first and subtracts the second should span the full mispricing range rather than half of it.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The two components are the archive's strongest validated results in their respective directions (+6.3% at t=4.94 and −5.4% at t=−5.09), and because each is near zero outside its own corner, subtracting them produces a monotone score whose extremes are the unforced-cheap and forced-rich populations rather than an uninterpretable mixture. This also repairs the flat cross-sectional slope of the short-side signal, whose low-signal region previously pooled cheap-and-safe firms with expensive-and-safe ones.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Claim Cheapness With Self-Funding Operations
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: If what protects a cheap firm is not the cash it has accumulated but its ability to fund its own cost base from current operations, then cash earnings measured against operating costs should gate the claim discount just as effectively as the cash balance does.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the sharpest available discrimination test of the mechanism the archive has uncovered: it keeps the units and the denominator of the winning runway gate but replaces the stock numerator with a pure flow, so a comparable alpha would mean the premium is about self-sufficiency in general while a weak result would confirm that the cash stock itself is what markets underprice. Since profitability screens scaled by assets have consistently produced only +1.7% to +2.4% on this leg, a strong result here would also show that the scaling, not the profitability, was the problem.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Additive Unforced Cheapness Score
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(SUMRANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(che, cogs)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheapness and freedom from forced transaction may be substitutes rather than complements — a very deep discount can compensate for a moderate runway and vice versa — in which case an additive score across the three ranked channels captures the mispricing with broader, more stable portfolio composition than a multiplicative gate.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The champion multiplies two ranks, which concentrates the long leg in the corner where both are extreme and may explain why its Sharpe (0.376) is high but its cross-sectional slope (3.86) is below that of simpler additive constructs in the archive. Testing the additive form of exactly the same three channels isolates the combination operator as the design variable, which is the one structural question the archive has never answered on its best-performing ingredients.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Claim Cheapness With Cash After Commitments---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The archive already contains gross cash (che/cogs, +6.3%), cash net of all current liabilities ((che−lct)/cogs, +5.0%) and cash against total debt (che/(dltt+dlc), +4.9%) on the identical valuation leg, so netting out dlc+dvc is a third interpolation point on the same continuum rather than a new mechanism, and the dvc term adds little since dividends are small relative to cogs for most firms.

---CRITIQUE Consensus Cheapness With Survival Horizon---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Merging the highest-slope leg (gross-profit yield) with the highest-alpha leg under the same runway gate is a substantively motivated attempt to resolve a documented FMB/alpha divergence, though the nested SUMRANK weights the claim channel roughly half and the two earnings channels a quarter each — not the "three equally weighted ranks" the reasoning claims — and gross profit and cash earnings are highly collinear, so the incremental information may be smaller than advertised.

---CRITIQUE Claim Cheapness With Extended Runway---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Converting the runway gate from a pure stock to stock-plus-flow is an economically sensible fix for the "buffer being drained vs replenished" blind spot, but MA(ib+dp,3) already drives the valuation leg, so the gate partly re-weights the same profitability variable and the expression risks becoming a quadratic in cash earnings rather than an independent conditioning state.

---CRITIQUE Unforced Cheapness Minus Forced Richness---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a mechanical linear combination of two already-evaluated archive signals rather than a new hypothesis, and the subtraction is not economically clean — the short component carried an insignificant FMB slope (t=−0.54) and both terms are non-negative rank products whose difference is dominated by whichever leg has the wider dispersion, so any gain would reflect portfolio blending, not a tested mechanism.

---CRITIQUE Claim Cheapness With Self-Funding Operations---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Holding the denominator and units of the winning gate fixed while swapping the cash stock for the cash flow is a genuine discrimination test that can falsify the "unforced transaction" story against a plain profitability-scaling story, and either outcome is informative; the main caveat is the shared MA(ib+dp,3) term with the valuation leg.

---CRITIQUE Additive Unforced Cheapness Score---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Isolating the combination operator (complements vs substitutes) on the archive's best ingredients is a legitimate structural question the archive has not addressed, but it sits close to a cosmetic re-parameterisation of the champion, and the nested SUMRANK again yields unequal channel weights that undercut the stated "three equally weighted channels" design.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Claim Cheapness Without Near-Term Maturities
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(MA(ADD(ib, dp), 3), MUL(prcc_f, csho)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Freedom from forced transaction can come from the liability side as well as the asset side: a cheap firm with no debt maturing within the year faces no counterparty who can compel it to refinance, sell assets or issue equity, regardless of how large its cash balance happens to be.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This leaves the cash-denominator continuum entirely and tests the maturity-timing channel on the long side, which the archive has probed only from the overpriced side where it worked strongly (current debt against cash, −4.5% at t=−4.32, and the asset-scaled funding gap, −5.4% at t=−5.09). Current debt scaled by total assets is defined for every firm, equals zero for the debt-free firms that the mechanism says should be most protected, and is not a rescaling of any cash ratio since a firm can be cash-poor yet free of maturities.
REASONING_END

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Excess Claim Per Dollar Of Annual Demands
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lt), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), ADD(cogs, dlc)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The economically meaningful quantity is how far a firm's unencumbered claim exceeds its market price relative to the annual demands that claim must satisfy; a large excess against small demands means the market is pricing the firm below a floor that nothing can force it to give up, while a negative excess against heavy demands means the price rests on nothing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Rather than subtracting two previously evaluated rank products, this expresses both tails inside a single monotone ratio: the numerator is signed and crosses zero exactly where the market price equals the unencumbered claim, and the denominator is the strictly positive sum of the operating and maturing-debt demands on that claim. It is structurally distinct from every recent archive entry, all of which are rank products, so it tests whether the mechanism survives without cross-sectional rank transformation, and its coverage is universal because all four inputs are reported by essentially every firm.
REASONING_END
